title: त्रिनवत्यधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Vasishtha says that through not awakening, the soul goes through crores of creations and falls. King Karala Janaka asks how the soul, which is said to be the same, is made of flesh and blood from mother and father, and the sage explains the mingling of the qualities in the qualities.
summary.kn: ಜಾಗೃತವಾಗದ ಕಾರಣ ಆತ್ಮ ಕೋಟಿಗಟ್ಟಲೆ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹಾದು ಬೀಳುತ್ತದೆಂದು ವಸಿಷ್ಠ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ರಾಜ ಕರಾಲ ಜನಕ ಒಂದೇ ಎಂದು ಹೇಳುವ ಆತ್ಮ ತಂದೆ-ತಾಯಿಯ ಮಾಂಸ-ರಕ್ತದಿಂದ ಹೇಗೆ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆಂದು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಋಷಿ ಗುಣಗಳು ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುವುದನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: वसिष्ठ कहते हैं कि न जागने से जीव करोड़ों सृष्टियों से गुजरकर गिरता है। राजा कराल जनक पूछते हैं कि जिस आत्मा को एक ही कहा जाता है वह माता-पिता के मांस-रक्त से कैसे बनी, और ऋषि गुणों के गुणों में मिलने का स्पष्टीकरण देते हैं।
summary.te: మేల్కొనకపోవడంతో జీవుడు కోట్ల సృష్టుల గుండా వెళ్లి పతనమవుతాడని వసిష్ఠుడు చెబుతాడు. రాజు కరాల జనకుడు ఒక్కటే అని చెప్పే ఆత్మ తల్లిదండ్రుల మాంసరక్తాల నుండి ఎలా అవుతుందని అడుగుతాడు; ఋషి గుణాలు గుణాలలో కలిసే తీరును వివరిస్తాడు.
summary.ta: விழிப்பின்மையால் ஆன்மா கோடிக்கணக்கான படைப்புகளைக் கடந்து வீழ்கிறது என்று வசிஷ்டர் கூறுகிறார். மன்னன் கராள ஜனகன், ஒன்றே என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஆன்மா தாய் தந்தையரின் ஊனும் குருதியும் கொண்டு எவ்வாறு ஆகிறது என்று கேட்க, முனிவர் குணங்கள் குணங்களில் கலப்பதை விளக்குகிறார்.
summary.ml: ഉണരാത്തതിനാൽ ആത്മാവ് കോടിക്കണക്കിന് സൃഷ്ടികളിലൂടെ കടന്ന് വീഴുന്നുവെന്ന് വസിഷ്ഠൻ പറയുന്നു. ഒന്നുതന്നെയെന്ന് പറയപ്പെടുന്ന ആത്മാവ് അമ്മയുടെയും അച്ഛന്റെയും മാംസവും രക്തവും കൊണ്ട് എങ്ങനെയുണ്ടാകുന്നുവെന്ന് കരാള ജനകൻ ചോദിക്കുന്നു; ഗുണങ്ങളുടെ ഗുണങ്ങളിലെ കലർച്ച മുനി വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.293; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: वसिष्ठ उवाच

meaning.en: Vasishtha said:

verses.text:
एवमप्रतिबुद्धत्वादबुद्धजनसेवनात् ।
सर्गकोटिसहस्राणि पतनान्तानि गच्छति ॥

meaning.en: Through such lack of awakening and by keeping company with the unawakened, a person passes through thousands of millions of creations, each ending in a fall.

verses.text:
धाम्ना धामसहस्राणि मरणान्तानि गच्छति ।
तिर्यग्योनौ मनुष्यत्वे देवलोके तथैव च ॥

meaning.en: Through his own radiance he goes through thousands of abodes, each ending in death, taking birth among animals, among humans, and likewise in the world of the gods.

verses.text:
चन्द्रमा इव कोशानां पुनस्तत्र सहस्रशः ।
लीयतेऽप्रतिबुद्धत्वादेवमेष ह्यबुद्धिमान् ॥

meaning.en: Like the moon in its phases, he is dissolved there again and again, thousands of times, through lack of awakening; such is the unwise one.

verses.text:
कलाः पञ्चदशा योनिस्तद्धाम इति पठ्यते ।
नित्यमेतद्विजानीहि सोमः षोडशमी कला ॥

meaning.en: The fifteen phases are called the womb and the abode; know always that Soma is the sixteenth phase.

verses.text:
कलायां जायतेऽजस्रं पुनः पुनरबुद्धिमान् ।
धाम तस्योपयुञ्जन्ति भूय एव तु जायते ॥

meaning.en: The unwise one is born again and again in a phase; they consume his radiance, and he is born once more.

verses.text:
षोडशी तु कला सूक्ष्मा स सोम उपधार्यताम् ।
न तूपयुज्यते देवैर्देवानुपयुनक्ति सा ॥

meaning.en: The sixteenth phase is subtle; let that be understood as Soma. It is not consumed by the gods; rather, it sustains the gods.

verses.text:
एवं तां क्षपयित्वा हि जायते नृपसत्तम ।
सा ह्यस्य प्रकृतिर्दृष्टा तत्क्षयान्मोक्ष उच्यते ॥

meaning.en: Having exhausted it, O best of kings, one is born; that is seen as his nature, and liberation is said to come from its exhaustion.

verses.text:
तदेवं षोडशकलं देहमव्यक्तसंज्ञकम् ।
ममायमिति मन्वानस्तत्रैव परिवर्तते ॥

meaning.en: Thus the body of sixteen parts, called the unmanifest, is thought of as "mine", and the person keeps revolving in it.

verses.text:
पञ्चविंशस्तथैवात्मा तस्यैवा प्रतिबोधनात् ।
विमलस्य विशुद्धस्य शुद्धानिलनिषेवणात् ॥

meaning.en: Likewise the twenty-fifth, the Self, through lack of awakening to it, though stainless and pure, comes by contact with pure air...

verses.text:
अशुद्ध एव शुद्धात्मा तादृग्भवति पार्थिव ।
अबुद्धसेवनाच्चापि बुद्धोऽप्यबुधतां व्रजेत् ॥

meaning.en: ...to be like the impure, O king, though its nature is pure; and even one awakened may become unawake through serving the unawakened.

verses.text:
तथैवाप्रतिबुद्धोऽपि ज्ञेयो नृपतिसत्तम ।
प्रकृतेस्त्रिगुणायास्तु सेवनात्प्राकृतो भवेत् ॥

meaning.en: Likewise, O best of kings, know that even the unawakened one becomes worldly through serving the three-qualitied Nature.

verses.text: करालजनक उवाच

meaning.en: Karala Janaka said:

verses.text:
अक्षरक्षरयोरेष द्वयोः संबन्ध इष्यते ।
स्त्रीपुंसोर्वापि भगवन्संबन्धस्तद्वदुच्यते ॥

meaning.en: This is held to be the bond between the imperishable and the perishable, as the bond between woman and man, revered one.

verses.text:
ऋते न पुरुषेणेह स्त्री गर्भं धारयत्युत ।
ऋते स्त्रियं न पुरुषो रूपं निर्वर्तयेत्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Without a man a woman here does not bear a child, and without a woman a man cannot bring forth a form.

verses.text:
अन्योन्यस्याभिसंबन्धादन्योन्यगुणसंश्रयात् ।
रूपं निर्वर्तयत्येतदेवं सर्वासु योनिषु ॥

meaning.en: Through their mutual union and reliance on each other's qualities, form is produced in this way in all wombs.

verses.text:
रत्यर्थमभिसंरोधादन्योन्यगुणसंश्रयात् ।
ऋतौ निर्वर्तते रूपं तद्वक्ष्यामि निदर्शनम् ॥

meaning.en: Through joining for pleasure, relying on each other's qualities, form arises in the fertile season; I shall give an example.

verses.text:
ये गुणाः पुरुषस्येह ये च मातृगुणास्तथा ।
अस्थि स्नायु च मज्जा च जानीमः पितृतो द्विज ॥

meaning.en: The qualities of the father, and those of the mother as well: bone, sinew and marrow we know come from the father, O brahmin.

verses.text:
त्वङ्मांसं शोणितं चैव मातृजान्यपि शुश्रुम ।
एवमेतद्द्विजश्रेष्ठ वेदशास्त्रेषु पठ्यते ॥

meaning.en: Skin, flesh and blood we have heard come from the mother. So, best of brahmins, this is taught in the Vedas and treatises.

verses.text:
प्रमाणं यच्च वेदोक्तं शास्त्रोक्तं यच्च पठ्यते ।
वेदशास्त्रप्रमाणं च प्रमाणं तत्सनातनम् ॥

meaning.en: What the Veda declares as authority and what the treatises teach, the authority of Veda and treatise is the eternal authority.

verses.text:
एवमेवाभिसंबद्धौ नित्यं प्रकृतिपूरुषौ ।
पश्यामि भगवंस्तस्मान्मोक्षधर्मो न विद्यते ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Nature and Spirit always bound together in this way, venerable sir, I conclude that there is no dharma of liberation.

verses.text:
अथ वानन्तरकृतं किंचिदेव निदर्शनम् ।
तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन प्रत्यक्षो ह्यसि सर्वथा ॥

meaning.en: Or else tell me truly some other example close at hand, for you see everything directly.

verses.text:
मोक्षकामा वयं चापि काङ्क्षामो यदनामयम् ।
अदेहमजरं दिव्यमतीन्द्रियमनीश्वरम् ॥

meaning.en: We too desire liberation and long for what is free of disease, bodiless, ageless, divine, beyond the senses, and without a master.

verses.text: वसिष्ठ उवाच

meaning.en: Vasishtha said:

verses.text:
यदेतदुक्तं भवता वेदशास्त्रनिदर्शनम् ।
एवमेतद्यथा चैतन्न गृह्णाति तथा भवान् ॥

meaning.en: What you have said, citing Veda and treatise, is so; yet you do not grasp it as it truly is.

verses.text:
धार्यते हि त्वया ग्रन्थ उभयोर्वेदशास्त्रयोः ।
न तु ग्रन्थस्य तत्त्वज्ञो यथावत्त्वं नरेश्वर ॥

meaning.en: You carry the texts of both Veda and treatise, O lord of men, but you do not know the truth of the text as it should be known.

verses.text:
यो हि वेदे च शास्त्रे च ग्रन्थधारणतत्परः ।
न च ग्रन्थार्थतत्त्वज्ञस्तस्य तद्धारणं वृथा ॥

meaning.en: One who is devoted to carrying texts of Veda and treatise but does not know the truth of their meaning carries them in vain.

verses.text:
भारं स वहते तस्य ग्रन्थस्यार्थं न वेत्ति यः ।
यस्तु ग्रन्थार्थतत्त्वज्ञो नास्य ग्रन्थागमो वृथा ॥

meaning.en: He bears a burden who does not know the meaning of the text; but for one who knows the truth of the meaning, his study of the text is not in vain.

verses.text:
ग्रन्थस्यार्थं च पृष्टः संस्तादृशो वक्तुमर्हति ।
यथा तत्त्वाभिगमनादर्थं तस्य स विन्दति ॥

meaning.en: Only such a one is fit to speak when asked the meaning of a text, for through reaching the truth he finds its meaning.

verses.text:
यस्तु संसत्सु कथयेद्ग्रन्थार्थं स्थूलबुद्धिमान् ।
स कथं मन्दविज्ञानो ग्रन्थं वक्ष्यति निर्णयात् ॥

meaning.en: But if a dull-witted person expounds a text's meaning in assemblies, how will that slow understanding explain the text with certainty?

verses.text:
निर्णयं चापि छिद्रात्मा न तं वक्ष्यति तत्त्वतः ।
सोपहासात्मतामेति यस्माच्चैवात्मवानपि ॥

meaning.en: A leaky mind will not state the conclusion truly; he becomes a laughingstock, even though he is a person of self.

verses.text:
तस्मात्त्वं शृणु राजेन्द्र यथैतदनुदृश्यते ।
याथातथ्येन सांख्येषु योगेषु च महात्मसु ॥

meaning.en: Therefore listen, king of kings, to how this is correctly seen among the Sankhyas and the great Yogis.

verses.text:
यदेव योगाः पश्यन्ति सांख्यैस्तदनुगम्यते ।
एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स बुद्धिमान् ॥

meaning.en: What the Yogis see is also followed by the Sankhyas; whoever sees Sankhya and Yoga as one is wise.

verses.text:
त्वङ्मांसं रुधिरं मेदः पित्तं मज्जास्थि स्नायु च ।
एतदैन्द्रियकं तात यद्भवानिदमाह वै ॥

meaning.en: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, bone and sinew: this, dear one, belongs to the senses' realm, as you have said.

verses.text:
द्रव्याद्द्रव्यस्य निष्पत्तिरिन्द्रियादिन्द्रियं तथा ।
देहाद्देहमवाप्नोति बीजाद्बीजं तथैव च ॥

meaning.en: From substance comes substance, from sense comes sense, from body comes body, and from seed comes seed.

verses.text:
निरिन्द्रियस्याबीजस्य निर्द्रव्यस्यास्य देहिनः ।
कथं गुणा भविष्यन्ति निर्गुणत्वान्महात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: How could qualities belong to this embodied great Self, which is without senses, seed and substance, being free of qualities?

verses.text:
गुणा गुणेषु जायन्ते तत्रैव निविशन्ति च ।
एवं गुणाः प्रकृतितो जायन्ते च न सन्ति च ॥

meaning.en: Qualities are born in qualities and enter into them again; so qualities arise from Nature, and yet are not real.

verses.text:
त्वङ्मांसं रुधिरं मेदः पित्तं मज्जास्थि स्नायु च ।
अष्टौ तान्यथ शुक्रेण जानीहि प्राकृतानि वै ॥

meaning.en: Skin, flesh, blood, fat, bile, marrow, bone and sinew: know these eight, together with semen, to be products of Nature.

verses.text:
पुमांश्चैवापुमांश्चैव त्रैलिङ्ग्यं प्राकृतं स्मृतम् ।
नैव पुमान्पुमांश्चैव स लिङ्गीत्यभिधीयते ॥

meaning.en: Male, female and neuter: these three kinds are held to be of Nature. The Self is neither male nor merely male; it is said to be "marked" only in appearance.

verses.text:
अलिङ्गा प्रकृतिर्लिङ्गैरुपलभ्यति सात्मजैः ।
यथा पुष्पफलैर्नित्यमृतवो मूर्तयस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Nature, which has no mark, is perceived through marks born of itself, as the seasons are always known through flowers and fruits, their embodiments.

verses.text:
एवमप्यनुमानेन ह्यलिङ्गमुपलभ्यते ।
पञ्चविंशतिमस्तात लिङ्गेष्वनियतात्मकः ॥

meaning.en: So by inference the unmarked is perceived, the twenty-fifth, my dear, whose being is not fixed among the marks.

verses.text:
अनादिनिधनोऽनन्तः सर्वदर्शी निरामयः ।
केवलं त्वभिमानित्वाद्गुणेष्वगुण उच्यते ॥

meaning.en: Without beginning or end, infinite, all-seeing, free of ailment, it is called qualityless among qualities only because of its sense of ego.

verses.text:
गुणा गुणवतः सन्ति निर्गुणस्य कुतो गुणाः ।
तस्मादेवं विजानन्ति ये जना गुणदर्शिनः ॥

meaning.en: Qualities belong to one who has qualities; how can there be qualities for the qualityless? So those who see the qualities understand it.

verses.text:
यदा त्वेष गुणान्सर्वान्प्राकृतानभिमन्यते ।
तदा स गुणवानेव परमेणानुपश्यति ॥

meaning.en: But when this one regards all natural qualities as his own, then he is truly said to have qualities, as seen by the Supreme.

verses.text:
यत्तद्बुद्धेः परं प्राहुः सांख्या योगाश्च सर्वशः ।
बुध्यमानं महाप्राज्ञमबुद्धपरिवर्जनात् ॥

meaning.en: What the Sankhyas and Yogis everywhere call beyond intellect is the great-minded knowing one, awakened by avoiding the unawakened.

verses.text:
अप्रबुद्धमथाव्यक्तं सगुणं प्राहुरीश्वरम् ।
निर्गुणं चेश्वरं नित्यमधिष्ठातारमेव च ॥

meaning.en: They call the unawakened and unmanifest the Lord with qualities, and the eternal Lord without qualities the overseer.

verses.text:
प्रकृतेश्च गुणानां च पञ्चविंशतिकं बुधाः ।
सांख्ययोगे च कुशला बुध्यन्ते परमैषिणः ॥

meaning.en: The wise, skilled in Sankhya and Yoga, seeking the highest, understand the twenty-fifth principle distinct from Nature and her qualities.

verses.text:
यदा प्रबुद्धास्त्वव्यक्तमवस्थाजन्मभीरवः ।
बुध्यमानं प्रबुध्यन्ति गमयन्ति समं तदा ॥

meaning.en: When those who fear states and rebirth are awakened, they awaken to the unmanifest as knowing, and bring it to equality.

verses.text:
एतन्निदर्शनं सम्यगसम्यगनुदर्शनम् ।
बुध्यमानाप्रबुद्धाभ्यां पृथक्पृथगरिंदम ॥

meaning.en: This example, subduer of foes, gives a right view and a wrong view separately for the awakened and the unawakened.

verses.text:
परस्परेणैतदुक्तं क्षराक्षरनिदर्शनम् ।
एकत्वमक्षरं प्राहुर्नानात्वं क्षरमुच्यते ॥

meaning.en: Each has spoken of the other this example of the perishable and imperishable: they call oneness the imperishable and manyness the perishable.

verses.text:
पञ्चविंशतिनिष्ठोऽयं यदासम्यक्प्रवर्तते ।
एकत्वं दर्शनं चास्य नानात्वं चाप्यदर्शनम् ॥

meaning.en: When this one who stands in the twenty-fifth acts rightly, oneness is his vision and manyness is non-vision.

verses.text:
तत्त्वनिस्तत्त्वयोरेतत्पृथगेव निदर्शनम् ।
पञ्चविंशतिसर्गं तु तत्त्वमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥

meaning.en: This is a distinct illustration of the principled and the unprincipled; the wise call the creation of twenty-five the principle.

verses.text:
निस्तत्त्वं पञ्चविंशस्य परमाहुर्निदर्शनम् ।
वर्गस्य वर्गमाचारं तत्त्वं तत्त्वात्सनातनम् ॥

meaning.en: They call the twenty-fifth's principle-less state the supreme example; the class of the class, conduct, the principle from the principle, is eternal.
